rows.description: The class laughs when I mispronounce a word. I feel small and hot. A wise adult says "everyone is learning". I can laugh gently or say "that is unkind". Laughter that hurts is not the same as laughing together.

rows.description: I laugh at a child who fell, because everyone else does. I feel part of the group but a little uneasy. A wise adult asks "how would you feel?" Laughing at pain is a habit copied from others and can be unlearned.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, humiliation, shame

rows.description: The teacher makes me stand and show my mistake to the class. I feel hot and want to cry. It is not my fault. Telling a parent helps, and a good school lets a child feel safe to make mistakes.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, mockery, shame
related mind states: sadness, humiliation, trust

rows.description: After I spill juice at a guest's house, my parent says "accidents happen, let us clean up together". I feel relieved and loved. A parent's calm response teaches me embarrassment passes and mistakes can be mended.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: humiliation, mockery, shame
related mind states: affection, embarrassment, relief, calm

rows.description: My parent says "why can't you be like your sister?" I feel less loved and angry at her. It is not my fault or hers. Wise parents avoid comparison and value each child's own strengths and pace.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, resentment, rivalry
related mind states: affection, anger, envy

rows.description: Papa compares me with the neighbour's child and I feel hurt and stubborn. I may stop trying. A wise child says "I feel sad when you say that". A wise parent apologises and encourages me on my own progress.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, rivalry
related mind states: sadness, resentment, hurt

rows.description: I compare my colouring with the girl beside me and feel bad because hers is neater. I want to hide mine. A wise teacher says "look how far you have come", turning comparison into pride in my own growth.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, resentment
related mind states: pride

rows.description: I see another child run fast and think "I want to run like her". I feel inspired and a little jealous. Wise adults help me ask "can you teach me?" and say each child is good at different things.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, resentment, rivalry
related mind states: admiration, jealousy

rows.description: On my first day I cry as Mummy leaves, then the teacher takes my hand and shows me the toys. I feel scared then a little safe. A warm, steady teacher makes school feel like a friendly place.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, dependence
related mind states: sadness, fear, trust

rows.description: I hold on to Mummy's dress and cry at the school gate. Separation is truly hard. Wise parents say a short kind goodbye, tell when they will return and do not sneak away. Lingering makes it harder.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, trust
related mind states: sadness
